napoveda.admins.api: Admin identities have no access to the public API, which contains no write endpoint. Signing in requires two codes from two consecutive time windows.
napoveda.admins.what: Identities with access to this console. An admin is a separate identity: it has no groups and does not pass user authentication. The last admin of a realm cannot be deleted, nor can their credential be revoked.
napoveda.apps.api: The key is passed in the Authorization: Bearer header and determines the realm. A request from an address outside the allowed ranges is refused with status 403 before anything is read; an invalid key with status 401, without distinction.
napoveda.apps.what: The registered applications of this realm and their access keys. Each key carries a list of allowed IP ranges it is valid from, and a switch for whether the application may see the reason for a refusal. Both can be changed without replacing the key. The server stores only the key fingerprint (SHA-256); the key itself is displayed once, at registration.
napoveda.audit.api: The trail is a side effect of the calls themselves; it is neither read nor written through the interface. It is stored per day in audit/YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl, one record per line, and deleted once the retention window passes. The detailed denial reason is available here only.
napoveda.audit.what: The audit trail of this realm, read-only. Every authentication and every write is recorded, including the actor and the operation. Secrets, codes and keys are never recorded.
napoveda.audit_aplikace.api: From the realm audit trail: API requests, user authentications (the application side) and requests from outside the allowed ranges. An invalid key does not identify a realm; it only appears in the service log.
napoveda.audit_aplikace.what: Every request an application made with a valid key: where it came from, what it was about and how it ended. Consecutive identical requests are merged in this view; the audit trail keeps each one.
napoveda.audit_spravci.api: From the realm audit trail: admin sign-ins, writes and session events. A change made outside the console (ssh, the library on the server) carries the actor operator and has no address.
napoveda.audit_spravci.what: Admin sign-ins to the console and every change they made in the realm, refused ones included. Changes are grouped under the session they were made in.
napoveda.audit_uzivatele.api: From the realm audit trail (authentication with purpose login or unlock). The client address is reported by the application in client_origin; the application server address is measured by the service and checked against the key's allowed ranges.
napoveda.audit_uzivatele.what: Every authentication attempt of a user: when, from where, through which application, what for and how it ended. Codes are never recorded.
napoveda.groups.api: The server expands the chain and returns it as a flat transitive closure in the principals field. The client does not compute nested membership.
napoveda.groups.what: The groups of this realm and their chaining. A group contains identities and other groups. The groups group:users and group:public are reserved, belong to every identity and cannot be removed.
napoveda.users.api: An application requests authentication of a user; the output is a verdict, a subject identifier and a flat list of principals. The response status is always 200 — a denial is a result, not an error.
napoveda.users.what: The identities this realm authenticates. Each holds its own credential (a shared TOTP secret), delivered to the authenticator app by a pairing token. Locking keeps the identity, its membership and its audit trail, and refuses every authentication attempt; deleting also removes group membership.
